newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Bad weather delays Tajik prisoner exchange.
newsitem.headline: Bad weather delays Tajik prisoner exchange.

text.p: Bad weather on Monday delayed a scheduled prisoner exchange between government and opposition in Tajikistan, the former Soviet republic devastated by a four-year civil war. Officials said it would go ahead on Tuesday.
"The exchange will definitely take place," Amirkul Azimov, secretary of Tajikistan's Security Council, told reporters in the capital Dushanbe. "This is a gesture of goodwill," he said.
The exchange, between Moscow-backed government forces and the country's armed Islamic opposition, builds on a ceasefire agreed at talks in neighbouring Afghanistan last December.

The exchange was set to take place in Tavildara, under the control of opposition guerrillas and about 220 km (140 miles) east of Dushanbe, but Azimov said bad weather had prevented a helicopter travelling to the town with 20 opposition prisoners.

There also appeared to be misgivings on the opposition side. One representative, who asked not to be named, told Reuters that the government had only agreed to hand over 19 of its people out of 31 he said were originally listed for the exchange.
The opposition says the government holds about 600 of its men while the government says the guerrillas are holding about 300 Tajik government troops.
Tens of thousands lost their lives in the bloody civil war and many more were made homeless in the remote, mountainous republic bordering Afghanistan and China.
